verdict.rationale: Keycloak is a self-managed server that operators run themselves. It can run from a container image or be installed on Kubernetes/OpenShift via its Operator. The docs direct users to switch to a production database such as PostgreSQL, and user data can stay in existing LDAP/AD or other stores through federation. Community users confirm running it self-hosted, on-prem and in their own cloud environments. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation in the pack on database configuration options and supported database vendors.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can control where the auth system and its user data run — self-managed deployment, private instance, or my own database

citations.quote: Run Keycloak from a container image.
Install the Keycloak Operator on Kubernetes and OpenShift.
Switch to a production ready database such as PostgreSQL.
Keycloak has built-in support to connect to existing LDAP or Active Directory servers.
You can also implement your own provider if you have users in other stores, such as a relational database.
not a bad choice as a self-hosted IAM solution
